narrative:
The 2020 Colorado Rockies entered the pandemic-shortened 60-game season with genuine optimism, and a blistering 4-2 July gave fans reason to believe. The offense showed flashes of life, most memorably when veteran Matt Kemp cracked a go-ahead double in late July, but the bullpen — led by an embattled Wade Davis — immediately exposed the team's fatal flaw: an inability to protect leads late in games. Davis surrendered back-to-back home runs in the same outing, a preview of the organizational dysfunction that would define the months ahead.

August brought a rude awakening. The Rockies stumbled to a 13-16 record as the pitching staff hemorrhaged runs at an alarming rate, posting an ERA of 5.59 on the season. Kyle Freeland, once the ace of the staff, couldn't find his footing, and opposing hitters feasted. The offense managed a respectable .716 OPS but the run differential told the whole story: Colorado was outscored by 78 runs, a chasm too wide for any lineup to bridge.

September offered brief moments of hope amid a 9-16 collapse that buried the season for good. Kevin Pillar's grand slam on September 4th was the high-water mark, a thunderbolt that briefly rekindled playoff dreams, but the bullpen undid the work almost immediately. Carlos Estévez became the face of late-game heartbreak, surrendering leads in multiple September outings, while Tyler Kinley's disastrous three-run homer allowed to Jared Walsh effectively extinguished any lingering postseason hopes.

The 2020 Rockies finished 26-34, missing the expanded playoffs in a year when more than half the league qualified — a damning indictment of a roster that scored too few runs and couldn't get outs when it mattered most. The season served as a painful inflection point for the franchise, raising serious questions about the bullpen construction, the starting rotation's durability, and whether the window built around Nolan Arenado had quietly closed.

chapters.title: Fast Start, Fragile Footing
chapters.description: The Rockies open hot in July, with Kemp sparking the offense, but Davis immediately reveals the bullpen's vulnerability by surrendering two crushing home runs in the same game.

chapters.title: August Unraveling
chapters.description: A 13-16 August exposes the rotation's fragility as opposing hitters hammer Colorado starters, with Freeland suffering a three-run home run that encapsulates the staff's struggles.

chapters.title: Pillar's Grand Slam and False Hope
chapters.description: Kevin Pillar delivers a grand slam that briefly ignites September playoff dreams, only for the bullpen to immediately surrender the lead and snuff out the rally.

chapters.title: September Collapse
chapters.description: A 9-16 September death spiral, fueled by Estévez blowing multiple late leads and Kinley surrendering a backbreaking three-run homer, buries the Rockies' postseason hopes for good.

chapters.title: Too Little, Too Late
chapters.description: Isolated bright spots like McMahon's solo shot provide fleeting optimism, but a season-ending double play in San Francisco merely tidies up the math on a lost campaign.
